title: Summer squash (yellow or green), fresh, cooked without added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash, also known as zucchini, are young fruits of the Cucurbitaceae family, typically yellow or green. When cooked without added fat they retain a delicate flavor, crisp texture, and very low calorie count, making them an excellent choice for healthy eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belong to the same family as pumpkins, melons and cucumbers.
Unlike most squash, zucchini can be eaten raw, but cooking without fat preserves the most nutrients.
Yellow and green varieties differ only in skin color; taste differences are minimal.
They are a staple in low‑calorie dishes because they contain virtually no fat or carbs.
In Japan they are called “kakuri,” while in Italy they are known as “zucchini.”

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: 100 g of fresh summer squash provide about 17 kcal, ideal for weight management.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect eye health and combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Pesticide residue
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, wash thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions can cause gastrointestinal discomfort due to high fiber content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Summer squash can be steamed, baked, stewed, or quickly sautéed in a non‑stick pan without oil. Slice into rounds, half‑moons or cubes and add to salads, soups, stir‑fries, omelets, or grain bowls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store squash in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, loosely wrapped in a perforated bag. They stay fresh for up to 5 days. Keep them away from ethylene‑producing fruits.
